P-03-001.claim: 3D spire-shaped silicon electrode array with multiplexing

P-03-002.claim: Combination of known elements; moderate obviousness exposure

evidence.finding: Utah arrays showed <25% functional yield in chronic rat implants vs >70% for microwire and Pt/Ir arrays
Utah arrays showed 1.5-3x increase in noise and 2.25-9x increase in impedance vs in vitro measurements
Single-unit active electrode yield decreased from 52.8±10.0% (week 1) to 13.4±5.1% (week 24) in rat motor cortex
Average Utah array lifespan 622 days in NHP; ~50% exceed 40% yield at 1 year; one implant lasted 9 years in human
evidence.value: 622 days avg NHP, up to 9 years human

evidence.finding: MEA SEPs had 357% higher amplitude than µECoG; SNR similar (21.3 vs 19.4 dB)

P-03-003.comparison_summary: 3D penetrating arrays (Utah) provide superior single-unit recording and higher signal amplitude compared to 2D surface arrays, but show lower chronic yield (<25% vs >70%) and higher impedance increase. Average lifespan: 622 days NHP, up to 9 years human.

escalation.reason: Evidence is internally contradictory: 3D arrays show superior signal (357% SEP amplitude) but inferior chronic yield (<25% vs >70%). The proposition as stated cannot be resolved to a single ESTABLISHED state without escalation.
escalation.recommended_action: Split into signal-quality and chronic-yield sub-propositions; escalate to domain expert for trade-off adjudication.

P-05-001.claim: Claim 1 anticipation — NOT anticipated by any single reference

evidence.finding: 2D array with multiplexing; lacks 3D penetrating architecture, elongated tapered electrodes, ≥1000μm length
Describes same 3D device but published AFTER filing (1991 vs 1989); does not fully satisfy multiplexing limitation (describes wire bonding, not integrated multiplexing)

P-05-001.final_assessment: Claim 1 is NOT anticipated by any single reference. Self-prior-art (Campbell 1991) is close but incomplete due to post-filing date and incomplete multiplexing limitation.

P-05-002.claim: Najafi & Wise 1985 is closest prior art (2D array)

P-05-004.claim: Obviousness — motivation exists but specific combination not evidenced pre-filing

evidence.finding: Clear motivation exists to move from 2D to 3D for lower currents, better spatial resolution, and access to deeper cortical layers
No pre-filing evidence of specific combination: 3D spire-shaped silicon + thermomigration isolation + integrated multiplexing
HIGH — moving from cortical surface (2D) to depth (3D) represents significant mechanism displacement

P-05-004.final_assessment: Obviousness risk is limited. While motivation exists to move from 2D to 3D, the specific combination of 3D spire-shaped silicon with thermomigration isolation and integrated multiplexing was NOT evidenced pre-filing. The 3D penetrating architecture is non-obvious.

P-06-003.claim: Only penetrating electrode array with FDA clearance for human use

evidence.finding: Utah arrays showed <25% functional yield in chronic rat implants; abiotic failure modes predominant
30,000+ aggregate days of human use with ZERO reported serious adverse device events
Documented recording longevity exceeds 8 years in human BCI participants
Iridium oxide metallization showed superior yield compared to platinum in intermediate term (months 3-12)
Utah arrays had highest impedance spike post-insertion (immune response) but comparable SNR to microwire arrays

P-06-005.biocompatibility_summary: Utah arrays show documented long-term biocompatibility with 30,000+ aggregate human days, zero serious adverse events, and recording longevity exceeding 8 years. Chronic yield declines over time (~2% per month) but remains functional for years.
